The review notes that at 14mm, the center sharpness is excellent wide open, but the corners are fair to good due to field curvature and some coma smearing. Stopping down improves corner sharpness, but the extreme corners never quite match the center performance. At 30mm, the center sharpness is very good at f/4 and reaches excellence at f/5.6, while the corners require stopping down to f/11 to improve, though diffraction may affect overall sharpness at that aperture. ([zsystemuser.com](https://www.zsystemuser.com/z-mount-lenses/nikkor-lenses/nikon-z-mount-lens-reviews/nikon-14-30mm-f4-s-lens.html?utm_source=openai))

Additionally, another review of the same lens mentions that at 14mm, stopping down from f/4 to f/5.6 and f/8 improves corner sharpness, with f/5.6 yielding pleasing results on close inspection. At 30mm, there is a perceptible drop in sharpness when used wide open, and stopping down to f/5.6 helps locate the lens's sweet spot. ([amateurphotographer.com](https://amateurphotographer.com/review/nikkor-z-14-30mm-f-4-s/?utm_source=openai))
